summary: Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Mahasi Sayadaw from around 1965 to 1970 and under Anagarika Munindra from around 1967 to 1980, and she taught Sylvia Boorstein.

Dipak Kumar Barua (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 1987, he served as a postgraduate dean at the University of Calcutta, and from circa 1996 to 2006 he held a post as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He was attested in 1994 as a faculty member in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.

Dipesh Chakrabarty (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD), he taught at the University of Melbourne (~1984–1995) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff (born 1938) is an Indologist and historian who earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University. He served at Leiden as a lecturer in 1967 and held the Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.

Diwakar Acharya (born 1969), an Indologist and philosopher, studied under Ramananda Giri and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (~2001–2004). He taught at Nepal Sanskrit University, Hamburg, Kyoto University (2006–2016), and became a professor at Oxford in 2016.
Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu from circa 1879 to 1882. He later served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at St. Petersburg University from around 1886 to 1890. He subsequently held an academic post at the Imperial University of Dorpat from circa 1898 to 1918.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous masters, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (~1944–1959) and Kunzang Pelden, and taught Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and others.

Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 1995 and also studied with Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. His career includes posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (2000) and EPHE (2005).

Dominic Sur works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia—under David Germano, Karen Christina Lang, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer—as well as under Khenpo Lama Chönam. He was attested at Utah State University in 2017.

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist educated at the University of London and the University of Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1985–2002), UCL (2002–2009), the University of Vienna (2009–2015), and the University of Alberta (2015).

Dominique Sportiche (born 1952) is a linguist who completed his studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology around 1979 to 1984. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1987.

Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University from circa 1990 to 1993. She was attested as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies in 2000.
Don A. Pittman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago. He was attested as a faculty member at Texas Christian University in 2001.

Don Handelman (born 1939) is a scholar in anthropology and religious studies who studied at McGill, Pittsburgh, and Manchester. He served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1972 to 2008.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) was an Indologist, historian, and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Geiger at Erlangen (~1894–1897). He served as epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1928) and worked at the University of London (~1917–1930).

Donald A. Ringe (born 1954) is a linguist and Indologist educated at Kentucky, Oxford, and Yale (PhD under Warren Cowgill). He taught Classics at Bard College (1983–1985) before joining the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald Capps (1939–2015) was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1970). He held faculty posts at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).
